The resignations are piling up in Perikatan Nasional, and if you thought the Perlis Mentri Besar drama was messy, the aftermath is turning into an absolute political circus. Muhyiddin's out, Azmin Ali's out, Faisal Azumu's out, and while some observers are trying to frame this as standard operating procedure, the timing and circumstances suggest something far more chaotic is brewing beneath the surface. Meanwhile, PAS is making its move, positioning itself to lead the coalition into what they're calling a "brand new era" of defending bangsa dan agama. The irony, of course, is that this power grab comes right after the very betrayals that supposedly justified all their unity rhetoric in the first place.

What we're witnessing is the spectacular unraveling of yet another chapter in Malaysia's ongoing saga of fake Malay unity. From PAS betraying UMNO to Bersatu's endless internal backstabbing, every possible permutation of political treachery has now been demonstrated. Youth leaders are complaining they weren't consulted, Akmal Saleh's Muafakat Nasional dreams look increasingly hollow, and the party that literally calls itself "united" can't stop fighting itself long enough to maintain even the appearance of cohesion. The pattern is clear: these politicians have been playing musical chairs with loyalty while wrapping themselves in the language of religious and racial solidarity, and now the music has stopped with everyone scrambling for whatever position they can grab.

The real question isn't just what's happening to Perikatan Nasional, but what happens to Malaysia if PAS actually succeeds in taking the reins. Because knowing how to gaslight people about unity while undermining each other at every turn is one thing, but actually governing a diverse, modern nation-state requires competencies that go far beyond religious rhetoric and performative solidarity. As this year draws to a close, we're getting a masterclass in why political movements built on nothing but identity politics and victimhood narratives inevitably eat themselves alive. The unity was always a fraud, and now everyone can see it.
